notes: Explosion during scheduled repair work between Kalinino and Yambakhtino, Vurnarsky District. Three gas service workers killed, one injured. Gazprom stated supply continued via parallel pipelines; no sustained throughput loss claimed. No attribution to hostile action.

Reactor unit shut down automatically after a turbine generator safety-system fault, reported by Rosenergoatom as a false alarm. Contributed to rolling outages across Krasnodar Krai and Rostov Oblast during a heatwave; DonEnergo attributed load stress partly to 39C+ temperatures. Capacity offline not quantified in open reporting.

Russia-Ukraine gas transit agreement of 30 December 2019 expired at 07:00 Kyiv time on 1 January 2025; transit via the Sudzha entry point ceased. Commercial and political termination rather than a sanction in the narrow sense - classified under the sanctions/supply-chain category because the taxonomy has no separate commercial-constraint class. Final pre-halt inflow recorded at 40.4 mcm on 31 December 2024.
Reported drone attack on the Kaleykino oil pumping station, a Druzhba transport hub in Tatarstan, attributed in reporting to Ukraine's SBU. Throughput effect not quantified in open sources.

Repeated drone strikes on the Unecha Druzhba pumping station in Bryansk Oblast during August 2025. Hungarian Foreign Minister Szijjarto confirmed Druzhba deliveries suspended. Day-level date not established across sources - recorded at month precision rather than inferred. Reports differ on the number of separate strikes in the month.

Crimea (internationally Ukrainian; tracked as a context unit, excluded from the Russia+Belarus ESDI). Ukrainian strike on 7 October 2024 on the JSC Marine Oil Terminal at Feodosia, the largest fuel storage facility in occupied Crimea. Satellite imagery reviewed by independent analysts showed 12 of 34 tanks hit, 8 completely destroyed. Multiple independent outlets plus satellite confirmation.

Electricity-sector event. Reported strike on the 750 kV Novobryanskaya substation in Bryansk Oblast; OSINT reporting cited ~500 MW of transmission throughput lost and a ~15% cut to electricity exports to Belarus. capacity_affected_mw here is transmission throughput, not generation removed, and is scored as an electric-power disruption with that caveat.

Electricity-sector event. Reported drone strike on the 110 kV Zheleznogorsk substation, Kursk Oblast, on 20 November 2025; ~16,000-20,000 customers reported without power. Customer-count effect only; no defensible generation-MW figure, so it is tracked and counted but not capacity-scored.

Electricity-sector event. Reported strike on the 110 kV Trubchevsk substation, Bryansk Oblast, ~October 2025; up to 15,000 residents reported without power, with hospital disruption and evacuations. Day-level date not firmly established across sources; recorded at month precision. Customer-count effect only, not capacity-scored.

Rosneft's Tuapse refinery struck in late January 2025, halting processing. Reuters (via industry sources) reported the primary crude unit CDU-12 repaired by late April and processing resumed around 6 May 2025 -- roughly three months. Recorded as a curated incident because the January 2025 strike is not enumerated at this date in the automated strike table; its observed reconstitution is carried in recovery.csv.

Generation event. Drone strike on 23 November 2025 hit high-voltage transformers at the ~1,493 MW Shaturskaya GRES (Moscow Oblast), causing a fire and interrupting distribution. Exposure links the plant's full installed capacity as capacity AT a disrupted site, not capacity proven lost.

Generation event. Reuters: a fire on 12 January 2026 at the ~2,214 MW Novocherkasskaya GRES (Rostov Oblast) took two units out of operation and briefly disrupted supply. Exposure links the plant's full capacity as capacity at a disrupted site; two-units-offline is not a clean MW figure so no capacity_affected_mw is claimed.

Transmission event. On the night of 20 August 2026 drones struck the 500 kV Taman substation in Krasnodar Krai, a main node of the energy bridge carrying power across the Kerch Strait; outages followed in occupied Crimea. Scored as transmission event-burden (weighted by 500 kV class), never as capacity offline.

Crimea context unit (internationally Ukraine; excluded from the Russia+Belarus index). Two drones struck an oil depot at Sevastopol harbour on 29 April 2023; four tanks burned (Ukrainian intelligence claimed 10+ tanks of Black Sea Fleet fuel destroyed). Admin-level only; no coordinates.

Crimea context. Reported strikes on the Zorya, Morske and Gaspra electrical substations on 19-21 July 2026 cut power to several occupied coastal towns. Admin-level region association only; no facility coordinates.
Crimea context. An electrical substation at occupied Feodosia was struck on ~28 July 2026, leaving much of the city without power. Admin-level only; no coordinates.

Overnight drone strike on the Orenburg gas processing plant (and the co-located helium plant), night of 23-24 June 2026. A fire was reported on the premises; extent of damage still being assessed. Strike confirmed by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

Overnight drone strike caused a fire at the Gazprom Astrakhan gas processing plant, 2-3 February 2025. Regional governor Igor Babushkin confirmed a UAV crash and fire on the premises, no casualties reported.
First reported drone strike on the Novoshakhtinsk plant, March 2024; refinery partially shut down after the attack.

Drone strike halted processing; governor said imported equipment was hit, with repairs estimated up to six months.
Reported struck in a coordinated multi-region overnight drone campaign, 29 Oct 2025.
Fire at a Naftan processing unit involving diesel fuel, Nov 2025; extinguished, no injuries reported. Not attributed to a strike.
Strike caused a fire that halted pumping via the Druzhba pipeline, 18 Aug 2025.
Druzhba pipeline dispatch station struck twice in about a week in late December 2024.
Struck in the mass overnight strike of 11 Mar 2025; Druzhba supply to Hungary reportedly stopped for repairs.
Strike on Stalnoy Kon; pumping via Druzhba reported halted, 7 Sep 2025.
At least three drones hit the Liskinskaya depot causing a large fire, 16 Jan 2025.
Drone strike took the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's largest Russian pumping station out of service, 17 Feb 2025.
Drone-debris fire on a fuel tank at the Adler depot; Sochi airport halted flights, 3 Aug 2025.
Drone strike caused a fire at the tank farm in Lyudinovo, 17 Jan 2025.
Drones hit two fuel-and-lubricant depots (Yartsevo, Razdorovo), 24 Apr 2024.
Drone strike ignited the state-reserve fuel depot at Engels; fire burned several days, 8 Jan 2025.
Drone struck a Druzhba pipeline site near Novozybkov; a technical building was hit, 30 Dec 2024.
Drone attack on the Sheskharis terminal briefly halted pumping; recovery work was reported largely complete within about two days, 14 Nov 2025.
Drone strike set Crimea's largest oil terminal ablaze, 6 Oct 2025 (first of two strikes in a week).
Second strike within a week; General Staff reported multiple fuel tanks damaged, 13 Oct 2025.
Overnight drone attack set the Hvardiiske oil base on fire, 17 Oct 2025.
Drone strikes reignited the Hvardiiske depot and hit storage at Simferopol, 29 Oct 2025.
Drone strike caused a workshop fire; plant suspended intake of Karachaganak gas, 19 Oct 2025.
General Staff confirmed strikes on the Orenburg gas-processing complex and Russia's only helium plant, 25 Dec 2025.
Governor reported a drone-debris fire; the stable-condensate motor-fuel unit was halted, 13 May 2026.
Overnight strike on the Novatek Ust-Luga terminals, 24-25 Mar 2026.
Drone hit the main building; brief local power problems, 23 Jul 2025.
Strike on the switchgear/boiler unit; hundreds of thousands lost heat and hot water, 6 Oct 2025.
Open-switchgear hit; city-wide outages and heat/water restrictions, 31 Oct 2025.
Explosions and fire at the large gas-fired thermal station, 6 Nov 2025.
Strikes on the Luch gas-turbine CHP and a city substation; hundreds of apartment blocks lost heat, 7 Feb 2026.
Downed-drone detonation damaged an on-site auxiliary transformer; a unit was reduced in capacity, IAEA reported normal radiation, 24 Aug 2025.
Governor reported a drone-debris fire and local outages, 16 Oct 2025.
Large fire at a key node in the Moscow-region grid ring; widespread outages, 31 Oct 2025.
Substation feeding Michurinskaya CHP disabled; power/water disrupted in Belgorod, 22-23 Feb 2026.
Drones damaged transformers/switchgear at two power-bridge nodes; blackouts, 12-13 Oct 2025.
